title: A Sociolinguistic Analysis of Automatic Speech Recognition Bias in Newcastle English

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing ASR transcription errors on spontaneous speech from the Newcastle English dialect (DECTE corpus), classifying misrecognitions by linguistic domain (phonological, lexical, morphosyntactic), and conducting acoustic analysis of specific vowel features to link phonetic variation directly to errors.
Comparing ASR transcription error rates and specific error types (e.g., lexical, phonological) between male and female speakers using generalized linear mixed-effects models (GLMMs).
Evaluating ASR error rates across different age groups (16-20, 21-40, 41-60, 61-90) to identify generational performance disparities in speech recognition.
Comparing ASR transcription error rates and error distributions across different socioeconomic categories (working class, middle class, retired, and students) using statistical modeling.
